script.content: The rain taps a steady rhythm against the grimy window of the detective's office. Arthur Cross sits behind his cluttered mahogany desk, a cup of lukewarm coffee growing cold at his elbow. The air is thick with the smell of old paper, dust, and cigarette smoke.
A knock at the door breaks the silence. It's a soft, hesitant knock—the kind that belongs to someone who isn't sure they should be here at all.
Cross sets down his coffee and calls out, "It's open."
Detective Cross? I'm sorry to disturb you. My name is Isabel Vance. I work at the Silvergate Museum. I... I need your help.
She steps inside, clutching her handbag tightly, rain glistening on her coat. Cross gestures to the chair across from his desk.
Sit down, Miss Vance. Tell me what's troubling you. And don't leave out any details—I find that people who leave out details usually end up regretting it.

Isabel sits down, takes a deep breath, and opens her handbag. She pulls out a yellowed photograph and slides it across the desk. It shows an ancient artifact—a golden amulet with strange symbols etched into its surface.

This is the Amulet of Serapis. It was donated to the museum last week by an anonymous benefactor. But I've been going through the archives, and I found a reference to it in a journal from 1923. The journal claims the amulet is cursed—that it brings misfortune to whoever possesses it. And last night... someone broke into the museum and tried to steal it.
Cross picks up the photograph, studying it intently. His eyes narrow as he turns it over in his hands.
A cursed amulet, a break-in, and an anonymous donor. That's quite a combination. What do the police say?

The police think it was just an ordinary burglary. But I know there's more to it. The symbols on the amulet... I've seen them before. In records from Blackwood Manor. The Blackwood family had dealings with occult collectors. I think the amulet is connected to the disappearance of Eleanor Blackwood.
Cross's expression hardens at the mention of the Blackwood name. He sets the photograph down and leans back in his chair.

choices.label: Investigate the Silvergate Museum
choices.description: Head to the museum to examine the crime scene and the amulet firsthand, starting with the site of the break-in.
choices.targetSceneDescription: Arthur Cross visits the Silvergate Museum to inspect the crime scene and examine the Amulet of Serapis. Isabel shows him around the museum and reveals more about the museum's connections to the Blackwood family.

choices.label: Visit Blackwood Manor
choices.description: Go straight to the source and investigate Blackwood Manor, the estate connected to the amulet and the disappearance of Eleanor Blackwood.
choices.targetSceneDescription: Arthur Cross travels to the outskirts of the city to explore the abandoned Blackwood Manor. The overgrown grounds and creaking halls may hold secrets about the Blackwood family's occult dealings and the amulet.

choices.label: Consult Mickey Donahue at the Docks
choices.description: Pay a visit to your old informant Mickey "The Fence" at his usual haunt near the docks, to see what the underworld knows about the amulet.
choices.targetSceneDescription: Arthur Cross seeks out Mickey Donahue at a seedy bar near the Riverside Docks. Mickey might have information about who is trying to steal the amulet and what it's really worth on the black market.

script.content: The Silvergate Museum looms before Arthur Cross like a marble mausoleum. Rain-slickened steps lead up to the grand entrance, where a uniformed security guard waits by the door. Isabel Vance is already there, her breath misting in the cold air.
Thank you for coming, Detective. The break-in happened in the Egyptian Antiquities wing. They disabled the alarm system—whoever it was knew exactly what they were doing.

She leads him through echoing marble hallways lined with glass cases. Ancient statues watch them pass with stone eyes. They reach a roped-off area where a display case stands empty, its glass shattered.
Cross kneels down, examining the glass fragments. He notices something—a faint smudge of dirt on the floor, leading toward a maintenance door.
The amulet wasn't the only thing in this case. What else was displayed here?
Just some papyrus scrolls and pottery shards. But look—I found this in the archives this morning.
She hands him a faded photograph. It shows a man in 1920s attire holding the Amulet of Serapis. The man has a familiar look about him—the same sharp jawline and piercing eyes as...

That's Augustus Blackwood. The patriarch of the Blackwood family. He was an archaeologist and occult collector. The journal I found suggests he believed the amulet could open a doorway to something—he called it 'the Veil Between Worlds.'
Cross studies the photograph, then looks up at the maintenance door. The smudge of dirt leads that way.

choices.description: Follow the trail of dirt through the maintenance door to see where the thief escaped.
choices.label: Follow the thief's trail through the maintenance tunnels
choices.targetSceneDescription: Arthur Cross follows a trail of dirt through the museum's maintenance tunnels, discovering a hidden passage that connects to the city's old underground network. He finds evidence of who might be behind the theft.

choices.description: Ask Isabel for more information about the Blackwood family's connection to the museum.
choices.label: Press Isabel for more details about the Blackwood connection
choices.targetSceneDescription: Arthur Cross delves into the museum's archives with Isabel, uncovering old letters and documents that reveal a secret society connected to the Blackwood family and a ritual involving the Amulet of Serapis.

script.content: A cab drops Arthur Cross at the rusted iron gates of Blackwood Manor. The old Victorian mansion rises from the overgrown grounds like a skeletal hand clawing at the grey sky. Ivy covers much of the stonework, and several windows are boarded up.
The gates groan as Cross pushes them open. A winding path leads through wild gardens where thorny bushes snag at his coat. The front door is a massive oak slab with a brass lion's head knocker.
To his surprise, the door swings open before he can knock. Standing in the doorway is a striking woman in dark clothing, her grey eyes cold and appraising.
Detective Cross. I was wondering when someone would come poking around. I'm Catherine Blackwood. This is my family's estate, such as it is. I assume you're here about the amulet?
Cross raises an eyebrow. He hadn't expected anyone to be living here.
You know about the amulet?
I know more than I'd like to. My family has been cursed by that trinket for three generations. Please, come inside. It's time someone heard the truth.

She leads him through a grand foyer filled with dust-sheeted furniture. Portraits of stern-faced Blackwood ancestors line the walls. They enter a study where a fire crackles in the hearth. Catherine pours two glasses of brandy.

My grandfather, Augustus Blackwood, discovered the Amulet of Serapis during an excavation in Egypt in 1922. He was never the same afterward. He became obsessed with the occult, convinced the amulet was a key to something he called 'the threshold.' My sister Eleanor disappeared ten years ago investigating his research. I've been trying to piece together what happened ever since.
She hands him a leather-bound journal, its pages yellowed and brittle.

This is Augustus's private journal. It contains details about the amulet and a ritual that he believed could tear open the Veil. I think whoever stole the amulet from the museum is planning to complete that ritual.

choices.description: Examine Augustus Blackwood's private study and search for hidden clues about the ritual.
choices.label: Search the study for more clues about the ritual
choices.targetSceneDescription: Arthur Cross searches the Blackwood Manor study more thoroughly, discovering a hidden compartment with maps, diagrams of occult symbols, and a list of names—seemingly members of a secret society that still operates today.

choices.description: Ask Catherine about her missing sister Eleanor and what she knows about the theft.
choices.label: Question Catherine about Eleanor's disappearance
choices.targetSceneDescription: Arthur Cross presses Catherine for more details about her sister Eleanor's disappearance. She reveals a shocking secret: Eleanor is still alive, and Catherine has been in contact with her. Eleanor went into hiding after discovering the truth about the secret society.

script.content: The Rusty Anchor is the kind of bar where the floorboards are sticky with spilled beer and the air is thick with smoke and secrets. Arthur Cross pushes through the creaking door, the bell above it announcing his arrival. A few hardened dockworkers glance up, then look away—they know better than to stare.
In a corner booth, nursing a glass of whiskey, sits Mickey Donahue. He flashes a yellow-toothed grin as Cross approaches.
Well, well, well. Arthur Cross. I was wondering when you'd show up. Word on the street is you've been sniffing around the Silvergate Museum. That's a dangerous game you're playing, my friend.
Cross slides into the booth opposite Mickey, signaling the bartender for a drink.
I'm looking for information about an amulet. The Amulet of Serapis. Someone tried to steal it from the museum last night. I need to know who wants it and why.

The Serapis Amulet? Oh, that's above my pay grade, Cross. Way above. But I hear things. There's a group—calls themselves the Order of the Threshold. Rich folks, old money types. They've been collecting artifacts like that for years. They believe in... how do I put it... opening doors.
What kind of doors?

Between worlds. Between life and death. I don't know the details, and I don't want to. But I can tell you this—the Order's leader is someone with a lot of influence. Someone connected to the museum. And they've been planning this heist for months.
Mickey leans in closer, lowering his voice.

If you want to know who's really behind this, you need to look at the museum's board of directors. One of them is a member of the Order. And I've heard they're planning a gathering—a ritual—on the night of the next new moon. That's three days from now.

choices.description: Investigate the museum's board of directors to identify the Order member.
choices.label: Investigate the museum's board of directors
choices.targetSceneDescription: Arthur Cross looks into the Silvergate Museum's board of directors, discovering a web of connections between wealthy families, the Blackwood estate, and the mysterious Order of the Threshold. He identifies a key suspect.

choices.description: Try to infiltrate the Order of the Threshold's gathering before the new moon.
choices.label: Attempt to infiltrate the Order of the Threshold
choices.targetSceneDescription: Arthur Cross uses Mickey's connections to try to get close to the Order of the Threshold, attending a secret meeting where he learns the true stakes of the ritual—and that the amulet may not be the only artifact they need.

script.content: Arthur Cross pushes open the maintenance door and descends into a narrow staircase. The air grows cold and damp as he goes deeper, the sounds of the museum fading away. The trail of dirt leads him through a labyrinth of service tunnels lined with pipes and electrical conduits.

The tunnel opens into a wider passage—an old underground corridor, its walls made of brick and mortar, clearly predating the museum itself. Victorian-era gas lamp fixtures line the walls, long since disused.

Cross finds a discarded matchbook on the floor. He picks it up. On it is embossed a symbol: an eye within a triangle, surrounded by arcane letters. Below it, an address: "The Thorn & Rose, 47 Crypt Alley."
Further along, he finds a footprint in the mud—a distinctive boot print, expensive leather, with a unique tread pattern. He takes a photograph with his pocket camera.
This isn't just a thief. This is someone who knows the museum's layout, knows the old tunnels beneath the city. Someone connected to that secret society Isabel mentioned. The Order of the Threshold.

choices.description: Investigate the address from the matchbook—The Thorn & Rose at 47 Crypt Alley, a likely meeting place for the Order.
choices.label: Investigate The Thorn & Rose tavern
choices.targetSceneDescription: Arthur Cross visits The Thorn & Rose, a dim establishment on Crypt Alley that serves as a discreet meeting place for the city's occult underground. He may find members of the Order of the Threshold or clues about their plans.

choices.description: Trace the unique boot print to identify the mysterious thief who broke into the museum.
choices.label: Trace the boot print to identify the thief
choices.targetSceneDescription: Arthur Cross uses his contacts in the city to trace the expensive boot print, leading him to a high-end shoemaker who remembers a very specific customer—one with ties to both the museum board and the Blackwood family.

script.content: Isabel leads Arthur Cross to the museum's basement archives—a vast, climate-controlled chamber filled with rows upon rows of metal shelving. The air smells of old paper and preservation chemicals.
She unlocks a cabinet marked "Blackwood Collection" and pulls out a dusty folder. Inside are letters between Augustus Blackwood and other members of what he calls "the Fellowship of the Threshold."

These letters describe a ritual. They believe the Amulet of Serapis is one of three keys needed to open what they call the 'Celestial Gate'—a doorway to another realm. The other two keys are a dagger and a crown. And according to these letters... all three were in the Blackwood family's possession.

Cross examines the letters closely. One of them mentions a hidden vault beneath Blackwood Manor where the items were kept. Another letter, dated just two months ago, suggests that someone has been secretly acquiring the keys.
Detective, I think the break-in wasn't a theft. It was a message. Someone wanted us to know the amulet was here—wanted to draw attention to it. They're setting something in motion.

choices.description: Return to Blackwood Manor to search for the hidden vault mentioned in the letters.
choices.label: Search Blackwood Manor's hidden vault

choices.description: Follow the trail of the thief who broke in by checking the museum tunnels.
choices.label: Investigate the tunnels beneath the museum

script.content: Catherine Blackwood leaves Cross alone in the study, saying she needs to make a phone call. As soon as she's gone, Cross begins a systematic search of the room.

He examines the bookshelves, running his fingers along the spines of ancient texts. One book catches his attention—a leather-bound volume with no title, tucked behind a row of Shakespeare folios. He pulls it out and finds it's a personal ledger.

The ledger contains names. Dozens of them. Prominent citizens: a judge, a newspaper publisher, a university professor, a police commissioner... and the director of the Silvergate Museum. Beside each name is a date and a transaction amount.
This is it. A membership roster for the Order of the Threshold. And payments—dues, bribes, or perhaps payments for artifacts.

Cross notices something else: the desk has a false bottom. He slides his fingers along the edge and finds a catch. A hidden compartment opens, revealing a map of the city with several locations marked in red ink. One of them is the museum. Another is the Riverside Docks. A third is marked "The Thorn & Rose." And at the center of it all, a large circle is drawn around Blackwood Manor itself.
Footsteps approach. Catherine is returning. Cross quickly replaces everything and steps back, his mind racing with the implications.

choices.description: Confront Catherine with the ledger and the map, demanding to know the full truth about the Order.
choices.label: Confront Catherine with the evidence
choices.targetSceneDescription: Arthur Cross confronts Catherine Blackwood about the ledger and map he discovered. She reveals that she has been trying to dismantle the Order from within, and that her sister Eleanor is in hiding because she discovered the Order's true goal: to use the amulet to resurrect a dark entity.

choices.description: Secretly copy the ledger and map, then pretend to leave—but tail Catherine to see where she goes.
choices.label: Secretly copy the documents and tail Catherine
choices.targetSceneDescription: Arthur Cross secretly photographs the ledger and map, then leaves Blackwood Manor without revealing what he found. He tails Catherine as she leaves the manor later that night, following her to a secret meeting of the Order of the Threshold.

script.content: Catherine Blackwood pours herself a brandy and settles into a leather armchair. Her grey eyes are distant, as if she's looking at something far away.
Eleanor isn't dead, Detective. She's alive. I've been protecting her for the past ten years.
Cross sits forward, his full attention on her.

Eleanor discovered what our grandfather was really involved in. The Order of the Threshold—they're not just collectors. They're a cult. They believe the amulet can open a gateway to the afterlife, allowing them to commune with beings from beyond. Eleanor found the ritual texts and realized they planned to use a human sacrifice—someone with Blackwood blood—to power the ritual. She ran. I helped her disappear.
Where is Eleanor now?

Somewhere safe. But I visit her. She's been researching the Order all these years. She believes the ritual requires three artifacts: the Amulet of Serapis, the Dagger of Nuit, and the Crown of Osiris. All three were hidden in a vault beneath this manor. But someone has been stealing them, one by one. The amulet was taken to the museum for safekeeping, but now it's been targeted too.

choices.description: Ask Catherine to take you to meet Eleanor in person, so you can learn everything she knows.
choices.label: Ask to meet Eleanor in person

choices.description: Search the manor's hidden vault to secure the remaining artifacts before the Order can claim them.
choices.label: Search for the hidden vault beneath the manor

script.content: Back in his office, Arthur Cross spreads out the information he's gathered. He makes phone calls, pulls old files, and studies the Silvergate Museum's annual reports. The board of directors is a who's-who of the city's elite.

He narrows it down to three individuals: Harold Pennington, the elderly museum director with a passion for Egyptian artifacts; Regina Ashford, a wealthy socialite and collector of occult curiosities; and Professor Alistair Moor, a disgraced academic who was once a consultant for the museum.

Cross digs deeper into Professor Moor. Ten years ago, Moor was involved in a scandal—he was accused of stealing artifacts from a dig site in Egypt. The charges were dropped, but his career was ruined. And there's a connection: Moor was a colleague of Augustus Blackwood.

He finds Moor's current address: a small apartment above a bookshop in the old district. But there's also a newspaper clipping—Moor was spotted at a private club called The Thorn & Rose just last week.
Pennington, Ashford, or Moor. One of them is the Order's mole in the museum. And whoever tried to steal the amulet knew exactly where to find it. That narrows it down to someone with inside access.

Cross checks the police report from the break-in. The alarm was disabled using a code that only senior staff knew. The list of people with that code is short: Pennington, Ashford, and two security chiefs. One of the security chiefs, a man named Victor Grimes, failed to show up for work today.

choices.description: Visit Professor Moor at his apartment above the bookshop to interrogate him about his connection to the Order.
choices.label: Interrogate Professor Moor
choices.targetSceneDescription: Arthur Cross visits Professor Alistair Moor at his apartment. The aging academic is paranoid and fearful, but reveals the Order's plan for a ritual at an abandoned church on the night of the new moon.

choices.description: Track down Victor Grimes, the missing security chief, before the Order silences him.
choices.label: Track down Victor Grimes
choices.targetSceneDescription: Arthur Cross hunts for Victor Grimes, the missing security chief. He discovers Grimes was paid off to disable the alarm, but now he's on the run—and someone is trying to kill him before he can talk.

script.content: Mickey makes a few hushed phone calls, then grins at Cross. "Alright, I got you an in. There's a meeting tonight at The Thorn & Rose. A private gathering of the Order. You'll need credentials."
He hands Cross a tarnished silver pin—an eye within a triangle, the same symbol from the matchbook.

This belonged to a member who won't be needing it anymore. Name's Edgar Finch—used to be a collector. Word is he died under mysterious circumstances. You'll be him for the night. The password is 'Threshold Eternal.' Don't forget it.
Cross pins the badge to his lapel and prepares to leave. Mickey grabs his arm.
One more thing, Cross. These people aren't amateurs. They've killed before. If they find out you're not Finch... well, the docks are a good place to dump a body. Be careful.
Cross nods, adjusts his hat, and steps out into the rainy night. The Thorn & Rose awaits.

choices.description: Attend the Order's meeting at The Thorn & Rose, posing as Edgar Finch.
choices.label: Infiltrate the Order's meeting

choices.description: Instead of infiltrating, stake out the tavern to see who enters and gather intelligence.
choices.label: Stake out the meeting from outside

script.content: The Thorn & Rose is a narrow establishment tucked between two crumbling warehouses on Crypt Alley. A faded sign swings in the wind, and the windows are painted black. Cross adjusts the silver pin on his lapel and pushes open the door.
Inside, the tavern is dim and smoky. A few patrons sit in shadowed booths. A man in a dark suit stands near a curtained doorway. He eyes Cross's pin and nods.
Threshold Eternal.
The man nods and parts the curtain. Cross steps through into a back room where a dozen figures in hooded cloaks sit around a candlelit table. At the head sits a figure in a silver mask.
The ceremony is tonight. The amulet has been secured. The dagger and crown await retrieval from the vault. All that remains is the blood of the Blackwood line.

The masked figure speaks with a voice that sounds strangely familiar. "Brothers, the new moon rises in three nights. We will gather at the old church on Crow Hill. Bring the artifacts. Bring the sacrifice. The Threshold shall open."
Cross realizes with a chill that the masked figure must have access to the Blackwood vault. Someone from inside the family is orchestrating this.

choices.description: Follow the masked leader after the meeting to discover their true identity.
choices.label: Follow the masked leader after the meeting
choices.targetSceneDescription: Arthur Cross follows the masked leader of the Order after the meeting ends, discovering their true identity and their connection to the Blackwood family.

choices.description: Alert the authorities and plan to intercept the ritual at Crow Hill church.
choices.label: Plan to intercept the ritual at Crow Hill
choices.targetSceneDescription: Arthur Cross gathers allies—Isabel, Catherine, and Mickey—to plan a raid on the ritual at Crow Hill church before the Order can complete their ceremony.

script.content: Cross takes the photograph of the boot print to a cobbler he knows in the old market district. Old man Higgins has been making shoes for the city's elite for forty years.
Higgins, I need you to look at this print and tell me who buys shoes like this.
Higgins examines the photograph through his magnifying glass. He whistles low.

That's a custom Italian leather Oxford. I've only made three pairs like this in the past year. One for Judge Morrison, one for the museum director Harold Pennington... and one for Professor Alistair Moor.
Cross's mind races. Pennington or Moor. Both connected to the museum. Both connected to the Order.

choices.description: Confront Harold Pennington, the museum director, about his role in the theft.
choices.label: Confront museum director Pennington

choices.description: Find Professor Moor and force him to reveal everything he knows about the Order's plans.
choices.label: Find Professor Moor

choices.description: Agree to help Catherine and Eleanor stop the Order once and for all.
choices.label: Team up with the Blackwood sisters
choices.targetSceneDescription: Arthur Cross allies with Catherine and Eleanor Blackwood to stop the Order's ritual. Together they plan to infiltrate the ceremony at Crow Hill church and use the Dagger of Nuit to disrupt it.

choices.description: Take the dagger and go to The Thorn & Rose to confront the Order directly.
choices.label: Take the dagger and confront the Order

script.content: Cross confronts Catherine in the study, laying out the ledger and the map on her desk.
I found these hidden in your study. Your grandfather's ledger. The map. You're part of the Order, aren't you?
Catherine's face pales, but she doesn't flinch.

No, Detective. I've been working against them. That ledger is evidence. The map shows their meeting locations. I've been gathering intelligence for years, waiting for someone I could trust to help me stop them. My sister Eleanor is alive. She's been hiding— researching the ritual and how to disrupt it.
She opens a hidden safe behind a painting, revealing journals, photographs, and a silver dagger.

This is the Dagger of Nuit. I removed it from the vault months ago. The Order doesn't know I have it. Without it, their ritual is incomplete. But they still have the amulet—and they're hunting for Eleanor, because they need Blackwood blood for the sacrifice.
Cross pretends to leave Blackwood Manor, but doubles back and finds a spot in the overgrown garden where he can watch the front door. He waits in the cold rain for nearly an hour.
Finally, Catherine emerges, wearing a dark coat with the collar turned up. She hurries down the path and gets into a waiting car. Cross flags down a cab and follows at a distance.
The car leads him through the city to a familiar address: The Thorn & Rose on Crypt Alley. Catherine enters through a side door, greeted by the doorman with a nod.
Catherine is a member of the Order. Or she's meeting them undercover. Either way, this is the place where answers hide.

choices.description: Follow Catherine into The Thorn & Rose to see what she's doing at the Order's meeting.
choices.label: Follow Catherine into The Thorn & Rose

choices.description: Wait and see who else shows up at the meeting, gathering intelligence from outside.
choices.label: Stake out the tavern from outside

script.content: Professor Alistair Moor's apartment is above a dusty old bookshop that smells of mold and mothballs. Cross climbs the creaking stairs and knocks on the door. A long pause, then a sliver of light appears as the door cracks open.
Professor Moor? My name is Arthur Cross. I'm a private investigator looking into the Silvergate Museum theft. I think you can help me.
The door opens wider. Professor Moor is a gaunt man in his 70s, with wild grey hair and haunted eyes. His apartment is filled with stacks of books and papers.
The theft. Yes, I heard. They've taken the amulet, haven't they? I warned them. I told Pennington that the amulet should never have been displayed. The Order has eyes everywhere.
You know about the Order. Tell me everything.

I was a member once. A fool's errand. I left when I realized they were serious about the ritual. The ceremony requires three artifacts and a sacrifice of Blackwood blood. They'll perform it at the old church on Crow Hill on the night of the new moon. You have three days. If you want to stop them, you need to find the other two artifacts before they do—the dagger and the crown. And you need to protect Eleanor Blackwood.

choices.description: Rush to Blackwood Manor to secure the remaining artifacts before the Order gets them.
choices.label: Secure the artifacts at Blackwood Manor

choices.description: Find Eleanor Blackwood and warn her that the Order is hunting her.
choices.label: Warn Eleanor Blackwood

choices.description: Take Grimes to safety and then confront Pennington about his role in the Order.
choices.label: Confront Pennington with Grimes's testimony
choices.targetSceneDescription: Arthur Cross brings Victor Grimes to safety, then confronts Harold Pennington at the museum. Pennington reveals that he is not the true leader—someone else, someone closer to the Blackwood family, has been pulling the strings all along.

choices.description: Secure Grimes and then go directly to The Thorn & Rose to gather more evidence.
choices.label: Secure Grimes and head to The Thorn & Rose

script.content: Victor Grimes's apartment is a dingy studio above a pawn shop. The door is unlocked. Cross enters cautiously, his hand near his coat pocket.
The place has been ransacked. Drawers pulled out, cushions slashed. In the bathroom, Cross finds Grimes—alive, but terrified, hiding in the bathtub behind the shower curtain.
Grimes? I'm not here to hurt you. I'm a detective. I need to know who paid you to disable the alarm at the museum.
Grimes trembles, his eyes wide.

It was Pennington. The museum director. He said it was a security test. Paid me five grand. But then I saw him at a meeting—at a place called The Thorn & Rose. With people wearing robes and masks. I knew I was in over my head. They've been looking for me ever since.
You need to come with me. It's not safe here. I know a place.

The meeting ends. The cloaked figures file out of The Thorn & Rose, dispersing into the night. Cross lingers near the entrance, watching as the masked leader emerges. The figure walks swiftly down Crypt Alley, turning onto a narrow side street.
Cross follows at a careful distance, staying in the shadows. The masked figure stops at a parked car—a sleek black sedan. Just as they reach for the door, the mask is lifted.

Cross's breath catches. It's Harold Pennington, the museum director. But then the figure turns, and Cross sees something else—a family resemblance. The jawline, the eyes. It's not Pennington. It's someone who looks like a Blackwood.
A Blackwood. But Catherine said Eleanor was in hiding. And Catherine herself... could she be lying? Or is there a third sibling?
Cross follows the car to a secluded mansion on the outskirts of town—not Blackwood Manor, but another estate. He notes the address: 12 Ravenwood Lane.

choices.description: Break into the mansion on Ravenwood Lane to uncover the leader's identity.
choices.label: Break into the Ravenwood mansion
choices.targetSceneDescription: Arthur Cross breaks into the mansion on Ravenwood Lane, discovering it belongs to a secret Blackwood relative—a cousin believed dead. Inside, he finds the Crown of Osiris and evidence of the ritual's true purpose.

choices.description: Return to Catherine and confront her about the mysterious Blackwood relative.
choices.label: Confront Catherine about the third Blackwood sibling
choices.targetSceneDescription: Arthur Cross returns to Blackwood Manor and confronts Catherine about the mysterious third sibling. She reveals the truth: her brother Thomas Blackwood, thought dead in a fire, is alive and has become the leader of the Order.

choices.description: Stage a raid on Ravenwood Manor to retrieve the crown before the ritual.
choices.label: Raid Ravenwood Manor for the crown
choices.targetSceneDescription: Cross and his allies stage a nighttime raid on Ravenwood Manor, where Thomas Blackwood has been hiding. They must retrieve the Crown of Osiris and confront Thomas before the ritual.

choices.description: Prepare a trap at Crow Hill church, setting up a fake ceremony to draw out the Order.
choices.label: Set a trap at Crow Hill church
choices.targetSceneDescription: Cross and his allies prepare a trap at Crow Hill church, using a fake amulet and the real dagger to lure the Order into a confrontation. The plan is risky but could end the threat in one blow.

script.content: Back in his office, Cross gathers his allies. Isabel Vance arrives first, followed by Catherine Blackwood. Mickey Donahue slips in through the back, a bottle of whiskey in hand. The office is cramped but the mood is determined.

The ritual is at Crow Hill church, three nights from now. They have the amulet. They need the dagger and the crown, and they need a Blackwood sacrifice. Catherine, you have the dagger. That's one piece they don't have. Isabel, you have the museum's records. Mickey, you have the street. We need to find where the crown is and stop them before they complete the ritual.

The crown was in the vault beneath Blackwood Manor. But when I checked last week, it was gone. Someone had already taken it. I think my brother Thomas took it—he's been presumed dead for years, but I believe he's alive and leading the Order.
I've heard whispers about a big meeting at a place called Ravenwood Manor. That's where the big players are gathering. If the crown is anywhere, it's there.

The ritual itself—I've been studying the texts. If they perform it with all three artifacts, they'll open a gateway. But if we can disrupt the ceremony at the right moment, or replace one of the artifacts with a fake... we could stop them permanently.

choices.description: Lead the sisters to Ravenwood Manor to confront Thomas before the ritual.
choices.label: Confront Thomas at Ravenwood Manor
choices.targetSceneDescription: With Eleanor and Catherine, Arthur Cross storms Ravenwood Manor to confront Thomas Blackwood. They must retrieve the Crown of Osiris and stop Thomas before he can complete his plan.

choices.description: Use Eleanor's knowledge to set a trap at Crow Hill church.
choices.label: Set a trap at Crow Hill church
choices.targetSceneDescription: Using Eleanor's detailed knowledge of the ritual, Cross and the Blackwood sisters prepare a trap at Crow Hill church. They will use a decoy sacrifice and the real dagger to destroy the artifacts and end the Order forever.

script.content: Catherine leads Cross down a hidden staircase behind the kitchen. The basement of Blackwood Manor is a labyrinth of stone corridors, lined with shelves of ancient artifacts and dusty crates.

At the end of the corridor is a reinforced door. Catherine unlocks it, revealing a small room where a woman sits reading by lamplight. She looks up—and Cross sees the resemblance to Catherine, but with softer features and tired eyes.
Detective Cross, meet my sister Eleanor. Eleanor, this is the man I told you about.
Eleanor Blackwood. Everyone thought you were dead.

I had to disappear. Our brother Thomas—he's the one leading the Order. He faked his death in a fire ten years ago. He's been gathering power, collecting the artifacts, waiting for the right moment. He needs me for the sacrifice. I'm the last of the direct Blackwood bloodline—Catherine inherited through marriage, but I carry the old blood.
Eleanor hands Cross a worn journal.
This contains everything I've learned about the ritual. The Order will meet at Crow Hill church on the night of the new moon. If we can get there first and set a trap, we can end this.
Cross finds Harold Pennington in his office at the Silvergate Museum, surrounded by artifacts and ancient texts. The elderly museum director looks up with surprise as Cross enters without knocking.
Pennington. I know about the Order. I know you paid Grimes to disable the alarms. I know about the ritual at Crow Hill. It's over.
Pennington's face goes pale, then hardens. He sets down his pen with deliberate calm.

You think you understand, Detective, but you don't. I'm not the leader. I'm a pawn. The true master of the Order is someone far more dangerous—someone with Blackwood blood. Thomas Blackwood. He's been pulling the strings from Ravenwood Manor. The amulet theft, the ritual—it's all his design.
Then you're going to help me stop him. Tell me everything about Ravenwood Manor and the ritual.
Pennington sighs, defeated. He opens a drawer and pulls out a detailed map of Ravenwood Manor, complete with security measures and the location of the vault where the Crown of Osiris is kept.

The ritual happens at midnight, three nights from now, at the old church on Crow Hill. Thomas will be there with the amulet and the crown. He only needs the dagger—and a sacrifice. If you want to stop him, you'll need to either get the crown first or set a trap at the church.

choices.description: Use Pennington's map to plan a raid on Ravenwood Manor.
choices.label: Use the map to plan a raid on Ravenwood Manor

choices.description: Go directly to Crow Hill church to set up an ambush before the ritual.
choices.label: Go to Crow Hill church to prepare an ambush

script.content: Ravenwood Manor is a dark Gothic mansion hidden behind tall iron gates on a secluded lane. Cross scales the wall and drops into the overgrown garden. The house looms before him, its windows dark except for a single light on the second floor.
He finds a side door unlocked and slips inside. The interior is opulent—velvet curtains, mahogany furniture, paintings of dark landscapes. He creeps upstairs toward the light.

In a study lined with occult texts, Cross finds the Crown of Osiris sitting on a velvet cushion. Beside it, a locked safe. He picks the lock and finds letters detailing the Order's final plan: the ritual will take place at Crow Hill church at midnight tomorrow. Thomas Blackwood will be there with the amulet.
The crown is here, but taking it now would alert Thomas. I could take it and run, or I could set a trap, or I could wait for Thomas to return and confront him directly.

choices.description: Take the Crown of Osiris and prepare to intercept the ritual at Crow Hill church.
choices.label: Steal the crown and prepare for Crow Hill
choices.targetSceneDescription: Arthur Cross steals the Crown of Osiris from Ravenwood Manor, forcing Thomas Blackwood to change his plans. The final confrontation moves to Crow Hill church, where the ritual will proceed with or without the crown.

choices.description: Wait in the shadows for Thomas Blackwood to return, then confront him directly.
choices.label: Ambush Thomas Blackwood at Ravenwood Manor
choices.targetSceneDescription: Arthur Cross lies in wait at Ravenwood Manor for Thomas Blackwood. When Thomas returns, a tense confrontation ensues that could determine the fate of the ritual and the Blackwood family.

script.content: Cross returns to Blackwood Manor and confronts Catherine directly in the study.
I followed the leader of the Order. He's a Blackwood. A man. I saw his face. It's not Pennington. Tell me the truth, Catherine. Who is he?
Catherine's composure cracks. She sinks into a chair, her hands trembling.

Thomas. My older brother. We thought he died in a fire ten years ago, but he survived. The fire was his plan—a way to disappear and build the Order in secret. He's been manipulating everyone: Pennington, the museum board, even me. He took the Crown of Osiris from the vault. He's the one orchestrating the ritual.
Where is he now?

Ravenwood Manor. Our family's old hunting lodge. That's where he's been hiding. He has the amulet and the crown there. The ritual is tomorrow night at Crow Hill church. If we're going to stop him, we need to act now.

choices.description: Rush to Ravenwood Manor with Catherine to confront Thomas directly.
choices.label: Confront Thomas at Ravenwood Manor
choices.targetSceneDescription: Cross and Catherine race to Ravenwood Manor to confront Thomas Blackwood directly. A dramatic showdown ensues as Thomas reveals his true plan for the ritual and the fate of the artifacts.

choices.description: Gather the Blackwood sisters and prepare a counter-ritual at Crow Hill church.
choices.label: Prepare a counter-ritual at Crow Hill
choices.targetSceneDescription: Using Eleanor's knowledge of the ritual, Cross and the Blackwood sisters prepare a counter-ritual at Crow Hill church. They will use the Dagger of Nuit to disrupt the ceremony and banish whatever the Order tries to summon.

script.content: Cross gathers his team outside Ravenwood Manor. Rain pours down as they check their equipment. Isabel has a map of the manor's layout. Catherine holds the Dagger of Nuit. Mickey has a set of lock picks and a revolver.
Everyone know their positions? Isabel, you cover the back exit. Mickey, you're on the front gate. Catherine and I go in for the crown. We meet back here in twenty minutes. No heroics.

They move in. Cross and Catherine slip through a basement window, navigating dark corridors until they reach the study. The Crown of Osiris gleams on its pedestal—but as Cross reaches for it, a figure steps from the shadows.
Thomas.
Thomas Blackwood stands before them, the Amulet of Serapis hanging around his neck. He smiles—a cold, calculating expression.

Catherine. I was wondering when you'd finally come. You have the dagger, I see. That saves me the trouble of taking it from you later. The ritual is tomorrow. You can either join me... or be part of it.

choices.description: Fight Thomas for the crown and the amulet right here and now.
choices.label: Fight Thomas for the artifacts
choices.targetSceneDescription: A violent confrontation erupts in Ravenwood Manor as Cross and Catherine fight Thomas for control of the artifacts. The struggle determines who will control the fate of the ritual.

choices.description: Retreat and let Thomas think he has won, planning to intercept him at Crow Hill church instead.
choices.label: Retreat and intercept at Crow Hill
choices.targetSceneDescription: Cross and Catherine retreat from Ravenwood Manor, letting Thomas believe he has the upper hand. They race to Crow Hill church to set a trap before the ritual begins.

script.content: Cross arrives at Crow Hill church hours before the scheduled ritual. The old stone building stands abandoned on a windswept hill, its stained glass windows shattered, its doors hanging askew.

He sets up the trap: a fake amulet made by Isabel from museum replicas, placed on the altar. The real Dagger of Nuit is hidden beneath a loose floorboard, ready to be used at the critical moment. Catherine and Eleanor hide in the bell tower, ready to spring the trap.

When Thomas performs the ritual with the fake amulet, nothing will happen. The gateway won't open. In that moment of confusion, Catherine will strike with the real dagger. The artifacts must be destroyed together to break the Order's power forever.
Hours pass. Then, the sound of cars approaching. Headlights cut through the darkness. The Order has arrived.

choices.description: Spring the trap as planned when Thomas begins the ritual.
choices.label: Spring the trap at the ritual's climax
choices.targetSceneDescription: The trap is sprung! As Thomas Blackwood begins the ritual with the fake amulet, Cross and the Blackwood sisters move to destroy the artifacts and end the Order's power once and for all. The final confrontation unfolds in the abandoned church.

choices.description: Reveal yourself before the ritual begins and try to reason with Thomas one last time.
choices.label: Confront Thomas before the ritual
choices.targetSceneDescription: Cross steps out of the shadows before the ritual begins, attempting one final confrontation with Thomas Blackwood. He tries to appeal to whatever humanity remains in Thomas, or force a surrender.

script.content: With Eleanor and Catherine at his side, Cross approaches Ravenwood Manor through the storm. Lightning illuminates the dark mansion as they pick the lock on the garden gate.
Thomas will be in the library. He always was. He'll have the amulet and the crown with him. He's been preparing for this his whole life.
Then we end this. Together.

They enter the manor silently. The air is thick with incense. Candles flicker in sconces along the walls. They find the library—and Thomas, seated in a high-backed chair, the Amulet of Serapis around his neck and the Crown of Osiris on a cushion beside him.

Eleanor. Alive after all these years. How touching. You've brought the dagger, Catherine. I was counting on it. Now the ritual can proceed as planned. Though I must admit, I didn't expect you to bring a detective.

choices.description: Confront Thomas directly and try to take the artifacts by force.
choices.label: Confront Thomas directly
choices.targetSceneDescription: Cross and the Blackwood sisters confront Thomas in a tense standoff. Words are exchanged, threats are made, and the fate of the artifacts—and the people who wield them—hangs in the balance.

choices.description: Use Eleanor's knowledge to perform a counter-ritual that will neutralize the artifacts wherever they are.
choices.label: Perform a counter-ritual to neutralize the artifacts
choices.targetSceneDescription: Eleanor reveals a hidden ritual she has discovered—one that can destroy the artifacts' power without needing to physically take them. But the ritual requires precise timing and a blood sacrifice.

script.content: Cross and the Blackwood sisters arrive at Crow Hill church hours before midnight. Eleanor leads them through the ritual texts, marking the positions for the counter-ceremony on the church floor with chalk and candles.

The Order's ritual is designed to open a gateway using the three artifacts and a blood sacrifice. But the same artifacts can be used to close the gateway permanently—if we reverse the ceremony. Thomas will bring the amulet and the crown. Catherine has the dagger. If we can get all three artifacts together at the right moment, we can destroy them and sever the Order's connection to the other side forever.
They prepare the ambush. Catherine hides in the rafters with the dagger. Eleanor positions herself behind the altar. Cross waits in the shadows near the entrance.

When Thomas begins the ritual, he'll be focused on the amulet. That's when Eleanor will signal, and I'll strike. Cross, you need to secure the crown. Without all three artifacts, the gateway cannot open.
The minutes crawl by. Then, at last, the sound of footsteps on stone. The Order arrives, led by Thomas Blackwood carrying the Amulet of Serapis and the Crown of Osiris.

choices.description: Execute the ambush when Thomas begins the ritual.
choices.label: Execute the ambush at the ritual's start
choices.targetSceneDescription: The ambush is executed as Thomas Blackwood begins the ritual. Cross, Catherine, and Eleanor move to secure the artifacts and stop the Order's ceremony in a dramatic, high-stakes confrontation inside the abandoned church.

choices.description: Step forward and try to talk Thomas down before blood is shed.
choices.label: Try to reason with Thomas one last time
choices.targetSceneDescription: Cross steps into the light and confronts Thomas directly, appealing to the brother he once might have been. But Thomas is far beyond reason, and the confrontation quickly turns dangerous.

script.content: Cross escapes Ravenwood Manor with the Crown of Osiris tucked safely in his coat. He races through the rain-slicked streets to Crow Hill church, where the Order is already gathering.
He bursts through the church doors just as Thomas begins the ritual. Without the crown, the ceremony falters. Thomas snarls with rage.
You think taking the crown stops me? I have the amulet. I have the dagger. I have the blood. The Threshold will still open!
But Eleanor and Catherine step from the shadows. Catherine holds up the Dagger of Nuit.

choices.description: Catherine drives the dagger into the altar, shattering both blade and amulet's power.
choices.label: Shatter the artifacts on the altar
choices.targetSceneDescription: Catherine drives the Dagger of Nuit into the altar stone, shattering both the blade and the amulet's power. The Order's ritual is destroyed.

script.content: Thomas Blackwood stands in the library of Ravenwood Manor, the Amulet of Serapis glowing against his chest. He holds the Crown of Osiris in one hand as Cross and Eleanor face him.
It's over, Thomas. The police are on their way. The ritual isn't happening.
You think I care about the police? I've been waiting ten years for this night. The Threshold will open. The Beings Beyond will reward my devotion.
Eleanor steps forward, her voice steady.
Thomas. Brother. I loved you once. But you've become a monster. Let me help you.
For a moment, something flickers in Thomas's eyes. Regret? Longing? The amulet pulses, and so does the tension in the room.

choices.description: Tackle Thomas and wrest the amulet from him before he can use it.
choices.label: Wrest the amulet from Thomas
choices.targetSceneDescription: Cross tackles Thomas and wrestles the Amulet of Serapis from him. The amulet is thrown into the fireplace, ending the threat. But Thomas's fate remains uncertain.

script.content: Cross and Catherine arrive at Ravenwood Manor to find Thomas waiting for them, seated calmly in the library as if expecting guests.
Catherine. I knew you'd come. But you've brought company. A detective. How quaint.
It's over, Thomas. The ritual is not happening. Give me the amulet.
Thomas laughs—a cold, hollow sound. He rises slowly, the amulet glowing against his chest.

You always were the sensible one, Catherine. But some doors, once opened, cannot be closed. I've already begun the ritual. The amulet is just a focus. The real power is in the blood. And I have all the Blackwood blood I need.
He draws a knife. But before he can act, Catherine hurls the Dagger of Nuit—it strikes the amulet, and both shatter. The power dissipates. Thomas falls to his knees, defeated.

*The Blackwood legacy of darkness ends here. Catherine rebuilds the family name. Eleanor emerges from hiding. And Arthur Cross closes another case, the mystery of the Serapis Amulet finally put to rest.*
At Crow Hill church, Cross, Eleanor, and Catherine prepare the counter-ritual. Eleanor draws the protective circles while Catherine holds the dagger. The Order arrives, led by Thomas.
Brother. I have studied the texts for ten years. I know the true names, the true patterns. The ritual you plan is a distortion. Let me show you what the Threshold was meant to be.
She begins to chant—not to open the gate, but to seal it. Thomas tries to interrupt, but Catherine blocks his path. The amulet glows, dims, and goes dark. The Order's members flee into the night.

*The artifacts are neutralized. The Order scatters. Eleanor and Catherine reconcile with Thomas, who surrenders quietly. The Blackwood family, fractured for a decade, begins to heal. And Arthur Cross returns to his office, ready for whatever mystery comes next.*

The old Crow Hill church is alive with candlelight and chanting. Thomas Blackwood stands at the altar, the Amulet of Serapis glowing with an otherworldly light around his neck. The Crown of Osiris rests on a velvet cushion beside the Dagger of Nuit—which Catherine has just handed over, playing her part in the counter-ritual.
Sister. You've brought the dagger. And the detective. How thoughtful. The blood of the Blackwood line, the three artifacts of power—tonight, the Threshold opens!
The moment of truth arrives. Eleanor begins the counter-chant. Catherine's hand tightens on the dagger. Cross watches the amulet, waiting for his cue.

choices.description: Watch as Eleanor's counter-ritual shatters the amulet and destroys the Order's power.
choices.label: Watch the counter-ritual succeed
choices.targetSceneDescription: Eleanor's counter-ritual reaches its peak, shattering the Amulet of Serapis and destroying the artifacts. The Order's power is broken forever.

script.content: Cross steps from the shadows of Crow Hill church, facing Thomas Blackwood directly as the Order gathers.

Thomas. I've seen the ledger. I know about the fire. I know you faked your death. But I also know that somewhere, beneath all this darkness, there's a man who loved his sisters. Don't let the amulet consume you.
Thomas hesitates. The amulet's glow flickers. For a long moment, brother and sisters lock eyes.
You don't understand, Detective. The things I've seen... the things I know... there's no coming back from that.
There is always a way back, Thomas. We're your family. Let us help you.

Thomas's resistance crumbles. He removes the amulet and hands it to Catherine. The Order dissolves without its leader. Thomas is taken into custody, but the Blackwood sisters visit him every month. *The case is closed—not with a bang, but with a family finding its way back to each other.*
The library of Ravenwood Manor becomes a battlefield. Cross tackles Thomas as Catherine grabs for the crown. Thomas throws a punch that Cross barely dodges, sending a bookshelf crashing to the floor.
Catherine retrieves the crown and smashes it against the marble fireplace. It cracks, ancient jewels scattering across the floor. Thomas roars in fury.
You've destroyed centuries of power! Do you have any idea what you've done?!
I've saved our family. That's what I've done.

With the crown destroyed, the amulet's glow fades. Thomas slumps in defeat. Cross calls the police. *The artifacts are no more. The Blackwood curse is broken. Catherine and Eleanor sell the manor and start anew. And Cross gets a new trench coat with his fee—the old one got rather torn in the fight.*
Cross and Catherine arrive breathless at Crow Hill church. Thomas has already begun the ritual. The air hums with energy. A shimmering void opens above the altar.
Too late, Detective! The Threshold opens! Behold the power beyond!
But Catherine knows the ritual. She knows its weakness. She steps into the circle and uses the Dagger of Nuit to cut the pattern—disrupting the flow of power. The void convulses and collapses.
The Threshold was never meant to be opened from our side. You were tricked, Thomas. The Beings Beyond can only come through if invited—you were their fool.

Thomas screams in denial as the gateway seals. The amulet cracks and falls to dust. *The Order of the Threshold is finished. Catherine and Eleanor begin a new chapter, using their knowledge to protect—not destroy. And Arthur Cross... well, he's earned a long vacation. But knowing him, he'll be back on the job by Monday.*
The library of Ravenwood Manor is a standoff. Cross faces Thomas, the Blackwood sisters flanking him on either side. Rain pounds against the windows.

Thomas, listen to me. The ritual doesn't open a gateway to salvation. It opens a gateway to something that will consume you. I've seen the true texts. Grandfather was wrong. The Beings Beyond are not gods—they are parasites.
Thomas wavers. The amulet dims. For the first time in ten years, doubt crosses his face.
Then what have I done? What have I sacrificed everything for?
You made mistakes. But you can still choose differently. We're your sisters. We'll help you through this.

Thomas breaks down. The amulet falls from his neck. Catherine picks it up and later delivers it to the museum's vault, where it will be studied—not worshipped. *The Blackwood family begins to heal. And Arthur Cross, standing on the steps of the manor as the storm clears, feels the weight of another case closed. The city sleeps easier tonight.*
Eleanor spreads the ancient texts across the library floor, marking the positions for the counter-ritual with candles and chalk. Catherine guards the door. Cross watches the windows.

The counter-ritual requires a blood price. A drop from each of us—Cross, Catherine, and myself. The three bloodlines that have been tangled in this mystery: the detective, the Blackwood sisters, and the innocent caught in between.
They each cut their palms and let their blood fall onto the ancient symbols. Eleanor chants. The air grows heavy. Far away, at Crow Hill church, Thomas cries out as the amulet's power drains away.

*The counter-ritual works. The artifacts are rendered inert. Thomas is found the next morning, confused and powerless, the amulet cold around his neck. The Blackwood sisters take him home. And Arthur Cross returns to his office, where a new client is already waiting. The work never ends—and neither does the mystery.*
As Thomas begins the ritual, Catherine drops from the rafters, landing silently behind him. Eleanor emerges from behind the altar. Cross locks the church doors from the inside.

Catherine presses the Dagger of Nuit to the amulet's chain and cuts it. The amulet falls. Eleanor catches it and smashes it against the stone floor. It cracks, ancient light spilling out before fading to nothing.
NO! Ten years! Ten years of planning—gone!
It's over, Thomas. The Order is finished. The artifacts are destroyed. You're going to prison—but maybe, with time, you'll find peace.

*The dawn breaks over Crow Hill. The Order of the Threshold is no more. Catherine and Eleanor walk away from the church, arm in arm, free at last. Arthur Cross lights a cigarette and watches the sunrise. Another mystery solved. Another story to tell.*
Cross steps into the candlelight of Crow Hill church, his hands raised. The Order members stir, but Thomas holds up a hand to quiet them.

Thomas, I've seen a lot of darkness in my line of work. But I've also seen people change. Your sisters love you. They're waiting outside. They want to help you. Don't throw away the chance to be a family again.
You don't understand. The things I've done...
Then let me understand. Help me understand. But don't do this. Don't become the monster the Order made you into. You're still a man, Thomas. You can still choose.

A long silence. Then, slowly, Thomas removes the amulet and places it on the altar. The Order members flee. Catherine and Eleanor enter the church, tears streaming down their faces. The three siblings embrace for the first time in ten years.

*The case of the Amulet of Serapis ends not with a clash of power, but with a family reunited. Arthur Cross tips his hat and slips out into the night. There will be other cases, other mysteries. But tonight, he lets the Blackwood family have their moment.*

Eleanor's counter-ritual reaches its peak. The amulet of Serapis glows blindingly bright, then cracks—once, twice—before shattering into a thousand pieces. The power that had been building for a decade dissipates like morning fog.
No... NO! The power... it's gone!
It was never yours to command, brother. The Threshold is sealed—for good.
The Order scatters. The church falls silent. Dawn breaks through the stained glass windows, casting fractured rainbows across the floor.

choices.description: Return to the detective's office, case closed, to reflect on the mystery that was solved.
choices.label: Case closed - return to the office
choices.targetSceneDescription: Arthur Cross returns to his office after the case. He reflects on the mystery of the Amulet of Serapis, the Blackwood family, and the secrets that still remain. A quiet, contemplative ending.

script.content: Cross lunges at Thomas, tackling him to the ground. The amulet flies from Thomas's grasp, skittering across the floor. Catherine snatches it up and hurls it into the roaring fireplace.
NO! After everything—after all these years—you think a fire can destroy it?
But the amulet does not burn. It sits in the flames, glowing. Catherine pulls it out with tongs and wraps it in a lead-lined box—the only thing that can contain its power.
It can't be destroyed. But it can be locked away. Forever. In a place no one will ever find it.

choices.description: Help Catherine seal the amulet in a hidden vault beneath Blackwood Manor.
choices.label: Seal the amulet in the vault
choices.targetSceneDescription: Cross helps Catherine seal the Amulet of Serapis in a hidden vault deep beneath Blackwood Manor. The artifact is locked away where no one will ever find it. A final, decisive ending.

script.content: Catherine drives the Dagger of Nuit into the ancient altar stone with all her strength. The blade meets the stone—and both shatter. A shockwave ripples through the church, extinguishing candles and sending Order members fleeing.
The dagger! The altar! You've broken the pattern—the gateway cannot form!
I told you, Thomas. The Blackwood women are not so easily broken. We endure.
Without the altar's focus, the ritual collapses. The amulet falls dark. The church grows still. Thomas is led away in handcuffs, the last member of the Order to be brought to justice.

choices.description: Enjoy the quiet aftermath of a case well-solved.
choices.label: Enjoy the quiet aftermath
choices.targetSceneDescription: In the aftermath of the Order's defeat, Cross shares a quiet moment with his allies. The artifacts are destroyed, the case is closed, and life returns to normal.

script.content: The detective's office looks different in the morning light. Dust motes dance in the golden beams that slant through the grimy window. The rain has finally stopped, and for the first time in what feels like weeks, the city is bathed in sunlight.

Arthur Cross sits in his worn leather chair, a fresh cup of coffee steaming beside him. The case file for the Amulet of Serapis lies closed on his desk, tied with a ribbon. He sips his coffee and watches the city wake up below.
There's a knock at the door. Cross doesn't move. Another knock, more insistent. He sighs, sets down his coffee, and calls out, "It's open."
Detective Cross? I hope I'm not disturbing you. I just... I wanted to say thank you. For everything. The museum is safe. The board has been cleaned out. And I've been promoted to head curator.
Isabel steps inside, no longer the nervous young woman from that rainy night. She carries herself with confidence now. She sets a small wrapped package on his desk.
It's a first edition. "Mysteries of the Nile" by Augustus Blackwood. I thought you might appreciate it. As a memento.

Cross unwraps the book—a handsome leather volume with gold lettering. He opens it and finds an inscription: "To Arthur Cross, who solved what the Blackwood family could not. With gratitude, Isabel Vance."
Thank you, Isabel. That means more than you know. How are the Blackwoods?

Catherine and Eleanor are renovating the manor. They're turning it into a museum—a real one, dedicated to debunking occult myths. Thomas... he's in a facility upstate. Catherine visits him every month. She says he's getting better.

Cross nods slowly, a quiet satisfaction settling over him. He looks around his office at the case files stacked on his shelves—each one a story, a mystery, a life. The work never ends. But for now, in this quiet moment, everything feels right with the world.

The Amulet of Serapis. The Order of the Threshold. The Blackwood family. It all started with a knock on my door and a photograph of a golden amulet. And here I am, back where I started—but the city is a little bit safer tonight. That's all I can ask for.

Cross picks up his coffee, takes a long sip, and settles back in his chair. The sun climbs higher over the city. Somewhere, a church bell tolls. Another case closed. Another mystery solved. Arthur Cross smiles, reaches for the morning paper, and enjoys the quiet.

The Blackwood Manor basement is silent save for the steady drip of water somewhere in the darkness. Catherine carries the lead-lined box containing the Amulet of Serapis. Cross follows with a lantern, its beam cutting through the ancient shadows.

They descend deeper than Cross has ever been beneath the manor—down a spiral stone staircase that seems to go on forever, through tunnels carved from the bedrock by hands long turned to dust. Catherine moves with purpose, as if she's made this journey a hundred times in her dreams.
My grandfather built this vault to hide his greatest treasures—and his greatest sins. The amulet will join them here. Forever.

They reach a heavy iron door covered in arcane symbols. Catherine produces an ancient key from a chain around her neck and unlocks it. Beyond lies a circular chamber, its walls lined with niches containing artifacts wrapped in cloth. In the center stands a pedestal of black stone.
Catherine places the lead box on the pedestal. She steps back, her breath misting in the cold air.
This is where it ends. Not with a bang, but with silence. The amulet will never see the sun again. The Order can find new idols, new delusions—but they'll never have this power.

Cross raises his lantern, casting long shadows across the chamber. He sees other artifacts in the niches—a bronze mirror, a set of bone dice, a circlet of twisted gold. Each one could be its own story, its own curse, its own mystery.
And what about you, Catherine? What will you do now that the hunt is over?

I'm going to live. Really live. Eleanor and I are going to travel—see the world beyond these manor walls. There's so much I've missed, hiding from the shadows my family created. It's time to walk in the light.
She turns to Cross, a soft smile on her face. For a moment, the weight of the Blackwood legacy lifts from her shoulders, and she looks younger—lighter.
Thank you, Detective. For not giving up. For seeing this through. You gave me back my future.

Cross nods, a rare warmth in his chest. Together, they seal the iron door, turning the key until the lock clicks with a finality that echoes through the tunnels. They climb back up toward the surface, leaving the darkness and the silence behind.

Above ground, the morning sun breaks over the Blackwood Manor grounds. Catherine and Eleanor stand together on the front steps, watching as Cross walks down the path toward the gate. He pauses, looks back, and tips his hat.
If you ever need a detective... you know where to find me.

Deep beneath the manor, in the darkness of the hidden vault, the Amulet of Serapis sits in its lead box, silent and contained. The Threshold remains closed. The Order's power is broken. And the Blackwood family—at long last—is free.

The Riverside Docks have never looked so peaceful. The morning sun glints off the calm water, seagulls cry overhead, and the usual shadowy figures are nowhere to be seen. It's as if the entire city took a deep breath and let it out.

Arthur Cross stands at the end of a wooden pier, a cigarette smoldering between his fingers. He's taken off his trench coat and draped it over a piling. For once, he looks like a man with nowhere to be and nothing to investigate.
Footsteps approach on the wooden planks. Cross doesn't turn around. He knows who it is.
Never thought I'd see the day. Arthur Cross, taking a vacation.
Mickey leans against the railing beside him, a bottle of whiskey tucked under his arm. He uncorks it and offers it to Cross.
It's not a vacation, Mickey. It's a strategic pause.
Mickey laughs—a rasping, genuine sound. They pass the bottle back and forth in comfortable silence, watching a cargo ship glide slowly out of the harbor.

You know, Cross, I've been running information in this city for thirty years. I've seen cops come and go, criminals rise and fall, and I've never—never—seen a case like this one get tied up so clean. You did good, kid.
Couldn't have done it without you, Mickey. Or Isabel. Or the Blackwoods. It took all of us.

Speaking of the Blackwoods—Catherine called me this morning. They're donating the manor to the historical society. She and Eleanor are opening a bookshop in the old district. Can you imagine? Blackwood sisters, selling books and drinking tea.
Cross smiles, taking another drag of his cigarette. The smoke curls into the clear blue sky.
Sounds like a happy ending to me.

They stand there for a long time, the two of them—the detective and the fence—watching the water and the gulls and the city stirring to life. No mysteries to solve. No conspiracies to unravel. Just a quiet morning at the docks.
Cross stubs out his cigarette on the railing and picks up his coat. He claps Mickey on the shoulder.
I'll see you around, Mickey.
You know where to find me, Cross. And hey—next time, try to pick a case that doesn't involve ancient death cults, yeah? My nerves aren't what they used to be.

Cross laughs—a rare, warm sound—and walks back toward the city, his hands in his pockets, the sun on his face. Behind him, Mickey takes another swig of whiskey and watches the detective disappear into the morning light. The case of the Amulet of Serapis is over. The city breathes easy. And somewhere out there, a new mystery is already waiting to be solved.

Detective's Office.name: Detective's Office
Detective's Office.vignette: A dimly lit room on the second floor of an old city building, filled with filing cabinets, a worn leather chair, and a mahogany desk cluttered with case files.
Detective's Office.appearanceDescription: A cramped but cozy office with walls lined by overflowing bookshelves and filing cabinets. A single dusty window looks out onto the busy street below. The desk is covered in papers, a half-empty coffee cup, and a vintage desk lamp casting a warm amber glow.
Detective's Office.backstoryDescription: Once a thriving private investigation agency, the office has seen better days. The detective took over the practice from their mentor, who solved the infamous "Midnight Heist" case here forty years ago. Now the walls are yellowed with age and the cases are smaller, but the office still holds secrets within its dusty files.

Silvergate Museum.name: Silvergate Museum
Silvergate Museum.vignette: A grand neoclassical building housing ancient artifacts from around the world, with marble floors and towering columns.
Silvergate Museum.appearanceDescription: An imposing three-story stone building with tall arched windows and a grand entrance flanked by Corinthian columns. Inside, marble floors gleam under the soft glow of chandeliers. Glass display cases line the halls, containing artifacts from ancient Egypt, Greece, and Mesopotamia.
Silvergate Museum.backstoryDescription: Founded in 1892 by the wealthy Silvergate family, the museum has been a cornerstone of the city's cultural scene for over a century. Recently, it has been plagued by a series of mysterious thefts that have baffled the police.

Riverside Docks.name: Riverside Docks
Riverside Docks.vignette: A misty waterfront area where cargo ships and fishing boats dock, a place of shadowy dealings and whispered secrets.
Riverside Docks.appearanceDescription: Weathered wooden piers stretch out into the murky river water, lined with rusted cranes and stacked shipping containers. Old warehouses with corrugated metal roofs stand like silent sentinels. The air smells of salt, fish, and diesel, and fog rolls in from the water most evenings.
Riverside Docks.backstoryDescription: The docks were once the lifeline of the city's trade, but economic decline has left them half-abandoned. Now they serve as a hub for smuggling operations and illegal dealings. The dockworkers union is known to be tight-lipped, and the police rarely patrol here after dark.

Blackwood Manor.name: Blackwood Manor
Blackwood Manor.vignette: An old Victorian mansion on the outskirts of the city, surrounded by overgrown gardens and iron gates that creak in the wind.
Blackwood Manor.appearanceDescription: A sprawling Gothic Revival mansion with dark stone walls, pointed turrets, and ivy creeping up every surface. Tall, narrow windows peer out like watchful eyes. The front door is heavy oak with a brass knocker shaped like a lion's head. The gardens are wild and untended, with thorny bushes and crumbling stone pathways.
Blackwood Manor.backstoryDescription: Built by the enigmatic Blackwood family in the 1870s, the manor has been the site of strange occurrences for generations. The last Blackwood heir vanished under mysterious circumstances a decade ago, and the estate has remained largely abandoned ever since—though local legend says the house is haunted.

Detective Arthur Cross.name: Detective Arthur Cross
Detective Arthur Cross.vignette: A sharp-eyed private detective in his late 40s, dressed in a rumpled trench coat and fedora, with a cigarette perpetually dangling from his lips.
Detective Arthur Cross.appearanceDescription: A weathered face with deep-set brown eyes that miss nothing. A graying stubble lines his jaw. He wears a battered brown trench coat over a waistcoat and tie, and a fedora that has seen better days. His hands are calloused, and he has a faint scar running down his left cheek.
Detective Arthur Cross.backstoryDescription: Arthur Cross was once a promising detective on the city police force, but a corruption scandal forced him out. Now he works as a private investigator, taking whatever cases come his way. He is haunted by the one case he never solved—the disappearance of Eleanor Blackwood, the heiress of Blackwood Manor. He is cynical but has a strong moral core, and will see a case through to the bitter end.

Isabel Vance.name: Isabel Vance
Isabel Vance.vignette: A nervous young woman in her mid-20s, wearing a modest dress and clutching a handbag as if it's a lifeline.
Isabel Vance.appearanceDescription: A pale, slender woman with auburn hair tied back in a neat bun. She has bright green eyes that dart around anxiously. She wears a simple blue dress and a beige cardigan, with sensible shoes. She carries a worn leather handbag that she holds tightly to her chest.
Isabel Vance.backstoryDescription: Isabel Vance works as a junior curator at the Silvergate Museum. She comes from a modest background and worked her way through university to earn her degree in archaeology. She is meticulous, detail-oriented, and deeply loyal to the museum and its collection. Recently, she discovered something in the museum's archives that has shaken her to the core.

Mickey \"The Fence\" Donahue.name: Mickey "The Fence" Donahue
Mickey \"The Fence\" Donahue.vignette: A wiry, fast-talking information broker who operates out of a seedy bar near the docks, knowing everyone's secrets and selling them to the highest bidder.
Mickey \"The Fence\" Donahue.appearanceDescription: A short, thin man in his 50s with a weasel-like face, slicked-back graying hair, and yellowed teeth. He always wears a cheap pinstripe suit that's too big for him, with a garish red tie. His fingernails are dirty, and he has a habit of rubbing his hands together when he's about to share a secret.
Mickey \"The Fence\" Donahue.backstoryDescription: Mickey has been a fixture of the city's underworld for thirty years. He started as a pickpocket, graduated to running gambling rings, and eventually found his true calling as an information broker. He has a photographic memory for faces, names, and secrets, and has survived this long by never getting too deeply involved in anyone's schemes.

Catherine Blackwood.name: Catherine Blackwood
Catherine Blackwood.vignette: A striking woman in her 30s, elegantly dressed in dark clothing, with a mysterious air and a sharp intellect that she uses as a shield.
Catherine Blackwood.appearanceDescription: Tall and slender with raven-black hair falling in waves past her shoulders. She has pale skin and piercing grey eyes that seem to look right through you. She dresses impeccably in black trousers, a silk blouse, and a long coat. She wears a silver locket around her neck that she never removes.
Catherine Blackwood.backstoryDescription: Catherine Blackwood is the estranged daughter of the Blackwood family, who left the manor fifteen years ago after a bitter argument with her father. She built a successful antique business in the city and has tried to forget her family's dark legacy. But when her brother vanished and her father died under mysterious circumstances, she inherited the manor—and all its secrets.

Eleanor Blackwood.name: Eleanor Blackwood
Eleanor Blackwood.vignette: A woman in her late 30s, worn down by years of hiding but still sharp-eyed and resilient, with a quiet determination in her voice.
Eleanor Blackwood.appearanceDescription: Eleanor has the same raven-black hair as her sister Catherine, but wears it shorter, practical. Her face is pale and lined with worry, but her grey eyes are bright with intelligence. She wears simple, practical clothes—a wool sweater and dark trousers—and moves with the quiet caution of someone who has been hiding for a decade.
Eleanor Blackwood.backstoryDescription: Eleanor Blackwood was the heir to the Blackwood family fortune and the one who first uncovered the dark secrets of the Order of the Threshold. When she discovered that her brother Thomas was the leader of the Order and planned to use her as a sacrifice, she faked her death and went into hiding. For ten years, she has been researching the Order's rituals and gathering information, waiting for the right moment to stop them.

Thomas Blackwood.appearanceDescription: A tall, broad-shouldered man in his 40s with sharp Blackwood features—raven-black hair streaked with grey, piercing grey eyes, and a cruel mouth set in a permanent sneer. He dresses in expensive black suits and wears the Amulet of Serapis openly around his neck. His hands are scarred from the fire he faked his death in.
Thomas Blackwood.backstoryDescription: Thomas Blackwood was the eldest child of the Blackwood family, groomed from birth to inherit the family's dark legacy. He became obsessed with his grandfather's occult research and formed the Order of the Threshold in secret. When his sister Eleanor discovered the truth, he faked his own death in a house fire and spent ten years amassing power, gathering the three artifacts, and preparing for the ritual that would open the Celestial Gate.
Thomas Blackwood.name: Thomas Blackwood
Thomas Blackwood.vignette: A charismatic and dangerous man who hides a fanatical devotion to the occult behind a veneer of aristocratic charm and cold intelligence.
